## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's localized surfaces currently resolve locale and fallback behavior in
separate implementations. Runtime and browser consumers therefore lack a small
shared contract for locale identity, explicit-versus-inferred precedence,
immutable render context, catalog validation, and reviewed English fallback.

This PR establishes that contract through one existing production consumer:
the onboarding wizard. It does not attempt product-wide localization.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the minimal foundation slice from RFC 0024:

- add the dependency-light `@openclaw/localization-core` package;
- register the existing 22-locale product union, aliases, fallback chains, and
  text direction;
- distinguish exact explicit matching from deterministic platform inference;
- resolve immutable localization contexts with source and audience provenance;
- render stable message descriptors through immutable catalog snapshots;
- support one bounded plural or select operation and reviewed English fallback;
- validate namespaces, key parity, placeholders, selector shape, and forbidden
  bidi controls in both English and translated catalogs; and
- migrate the existing wizard locale resolver and renderer without changing its
  catalogs or English output.

The Portuguese `pt-PT` to `pt-BR` platform inference is an explicit compatibility
rule preserving existing Control UI behavior, not a generic same-language
regional fallback.

The earlier cumulative draft also contained coverage governance, CLI adoption,
Gateway metadata, approval/safety presentation, and Control UI migration. Those
have been removed from this PR and remain independent owner-reviewed slices.

## User Impact

Onboarding keeps its existing English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional
Chinese output while gaining consistent locale normalization and fallback.
For example, `zh-Hant-HK` selects the existing `zh-TW` wizard catalog, while an
invalid explicit `OPENCLAW_LOCALE` falls directly to reviewed English instead
of silently using a host locale.

No command names, flags, config keys, protocol fields, structured output, or
translation catalogs change in this PR.

## Evidence

Exact head: `8db13b6a306c0559a6a627143058cf349ecdfe74`

- `git diff --check` passes across the exact 18-file diff.
- `oxfmt --check` passes for all 15 formatter-supported changed files.
- 43 localization-core, 16 wizard localization, and 19 dev-watch
  integration tests pass on Linux under WSL (78 tests total).
- `pnpm build` passes, including `tsdown` for the new workspace package,
  CLI bootstrap imports, runtime postbuild, plugin SDK exports, and Control UI.
- The three-line wizard source demonstration below was rerun unchanged on this
  exact head.

Blacksmith Testbox and brokered AWS Crabbox were attempted first but rejected
before repository code executed: the local Blacksmith CLI is authenticated to a
different organization, and the configured broker token returns HTTP 401. Per
trusted-source fallback policy, the proof above ran in an isolated Ubuntu 24.04
WSL worktree with lockfile-pinned dependencies.

The diff remains 18 files, 1,274 additions, and 44 deletions. The previous draft
was 67 files and 5,487 additions.
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
The existing onboarding wizard resolves normalized explicit locale aliases
through the shared kernel and preserves English fallback for invalid explicit
overrides.

Real environment tested:
Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Node.js 24.15.0, exact OpenClaw source head
`8db13b6a306c0559a6a627143058cf349ecdfe74`, using the source wizard renderer
with its shipped English, `zh-CN`, and `zh-TW` catalogs. No Gateway or external
service was involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run the wizard source renderer with `OPENCLAW_LOCALE=zh-Hant-HK` and render
   `wizard.gateway.port` plus an interpolated provider message.
2. Run the same renderer with `OPENCLAW_LOCALE=xx-invalid LC_ALL=zh-CN` and
   render `wizard.gateway.port`.

Evidence after fix:

```text
Gateway 連接埠
端點 ID "custom" 已用於不同的基礎 URL。將使用 "custom-2"。
Gateway port
```

Observed result after fix:
The `zh-Hant-HK` alias rendered the existing Traditional Chinese catalog and
preserved literal endpoint IDs. The invalid explicit locale ignored the
otherwise valid `LC_ALL=zh-CN` host input and rendered the reviewed English
fallback, matching the explicit-override contract.

What was not tested:
No Control UI, Gateway, channel, native-app, or external plugin behavior is in
this slice. Full root typecheck remains blocked by the two unrelated failures
listed above.

target.title: fix(zai,amazon-bedrock-mantle): reject invalid UTF-8 in extension API response JSON
target.body:
## Summary

Decode Z.AI probe error bodies and Amazon Bedrock Mantle model discovery responses with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so malformed UTF-8 bytes throw immediately, instead of silently becoming U+FFFD inside decoded JSON.

## What Problem This Solves

Two extension API response decoders used a forgiving `TextDecoder()` (default `fatal: false`), so invalid byte sequences silently became U+FFFD:

- **Z.AI probe** (`extensions/zai/detect.ts`): error bodies from the Z.AI chat completions API are decoded and JSON-parsed to extract error codes for endpoint classification. With forgiving decode, a corrupted byte becomes U+FFFD inside the error code string — the probe may misclassify the error.
- **Mantle discovery** (`extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.ts`): model discovery responses from the Bedrock Mantle `/v1/models` endpoint are decoded and JSON-parsed. With forgiving decode, corrupted model IDs/fields become U+FFFD strings — a silently corrupted model may be presented to the user.

Both were using `JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes))` without UTF-8 validation.

## Root Cause

Per the WHATWG Encoding standard, `TextDecoder()` defaults to `fatal: false`, which substitutes U+FFFD for malformed sequences instead of throwing. For API response JSON, this is the wrong default — API responses are expected to be valid UTF-8, and silent corruption hides real problems.

## Why This Fix

Add `{ fatal: true }` to the decoder in both locations:

- **Z.AI probe**: The existing inner try/catch already swallows parse errors and degrades to status-only classification — the `TypeError` from fatal decode is caught by the same path, fully backward compatible.
- **Mantle discovery**: Added a try/catch around the fatal decode that throws with a clear `"Mantle model discovery response is malformed JSON"` message; the caller (`discoverMantleModels`) already has a catch block that logs the error and returns cached/empty models.

This is the same strict-decode pattern already used in `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:344`, `src/commands/docs.ts:87`, `src/agents/mcp-app-sandbox.ts:106`, and across the `src/infra/` state migration decoders.

## User Impact

- **Before**: corrupted API responses could produce silently malformed model IDs or error classifications containing U+FFFD, with no error surfaced.
- **After**: corrupted responses are reported as malformed JSON errors (logged or swallowed with graceful degradation), and nothing corrupted propagates to user-visible state.

## Evidence

Tests added:

- `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts`: probe receives a 400 error body containing `0xFF` — the probe returns `null` without throwing, proving the fatal decode error is swallowed and the probe degrades to status-only classification.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts`: discovery receives a 200 response body containing `0xFF` — `discoverMantleModels` returns `[]` without throwing, proving the corrupted response is handled gracefully.

All existing tests pass without modification.

target.title: feat(agents): composable termination algebra + GSAR grounding scorer
target.body:
Closes #77981

## What this does

Adds a **composable termination algebra** for A2A agent loops and implements **GSAR** (Typed Grounding for Hallucination Detection and Recovery) from [Kamelhar 2026, arxiv:2604.23366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23366) as a first-class `TerminationCondition`. Both ship as **standalone, composable primitives** (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`) with full unit + live-API coverage.

> **Scope (updated):** this PR is **library/groundwork only**. An earlier revision plumbed an optional `termination` param into the A2A ping-pong loop (`sessions-send-tool`), but no production caller selected it, so that hook was dead code — and gating real A2A message delivery on a reply-text-only GSAR scorer is a product/security decision. The dormant hook has been removed; wiring the policy through a real `sessions_send` entry point, with a trusted-evidence GSAR contract (retrieved sources, not self-tagged reply text), is deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up.

---

## Proof 1 — the algebra saves turns

```
Task: "Where is the nearest coffee shop?"

WITHOUT algebra   MaxIterations(5)
  Claude  ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  (had the answer at turn 2, we waited anyway)
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns

WITH algebra   TextMention("FOUND IT").or(MaxIterations(5))
  Claude  ▓▓░░░  2 turns  ← "Blue Bottle on Mission St. FOUND IT"  ✓ EXIT
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  ← never says FOUND IT → MaxIterations saves it

  saved: 3 turns = 60% less waiting for Claude
```

Claude naturally signals completion. GPT does not. The combinator captures this difference without any provider-specific code.

---

## Proof 2 — soft signals must be paired with a hard bound

```
soft_signal                        ✗  UNSAFE — may never stop
soft_signal.or(MaxIterations(N))   ✓  SAFE   — always terminates
```

Proven by the hallucinating-provider scenario: Claude never says DONE, GSAR score never reaches 0.80 — `MaxIterations` fires at turn 5 every time. Budget holds.

The AND combinator lets you guard against vague early answers:

```typescript
const detailed = new CustomCondition(s => [s.replyText.length >= 40, "detailed_enough"]);
const cond = new TextMention("FOUND IT").and(detailed).or(new MaxIterations(5));
// turn 1: "FOUND IT!" — too short, fails `detailed`
// turn 2: "Blue Bottle on Mission St, 4 min walk. FOUND IT" — passes both ✓
```

---

## Proof 3 — GSAR score formula (arxiv:2604.23366 §3.2)

```
        W(G) + W(K)
S = ─────────────────────────    ∈ [0, 1]
     W(G) + W(U) + ρ·W(X) + W(K)

G = grounded   U = ungrounded   X = contradicted   K = complementary
```

**6 structural properties proven in the suite:**

| Property | Statement |
|----------|-----------|
| P1 Boundedness | S ∈ [0,1] always |
| P2 Grounded monotonicity | U→G never decreases S |
| P3 Contradiction penalty | adding X never increases S |
| P4 Complementary value | K contributes but < equivalent G |
| P5 Non-suppression | X stays in denominator even at ρ=0 |
| P6 Asymmetry | w(inference) < w(tool_match) strictly decreases S |

---

## Proof 4 — GSAR decision tiers and threshold stability

```
score   0.0──────────0.65──────────0.80──────────1.0
              replan      regenerate      proceed
                                   ▲
                             τ_proceed = 0.80 sits on a
                             ≥85%-accuracy plateau across [0.75, 0.85]
                             not a cliff — safe to ship as default
```

`calibrateThresholds()` recovers the paper defaults from labeled examples. Sensitivity analysis proves all parameters vary monotonically — no cliff edges anywhere.

---

## Proof 5 — GSAR wired into a recovery loop

```typescript
// Algorithm 1 from the paper — bounded recovery, termination guaranteed
new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))
```

| Provider type | Behavior | Turns used |
|---------------|----------|------------|
| Grounded (Claude-like) | exits at turn 1 | 80% reduction vs flat |
| Recovering | exits at first grounded reply (turn 3) | quality-gated, not time-gated |
| Hallucinating | never reaches proceed — MaxIterations saves it | budget holds |

---

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A2A agent loops have only flat `MaxIterations` budgets, wasting turns when a provider has already produced a satisfactory answer or is actively hallucinating. This PR adds the reusable primitives that fix that — delivered as standalone library modules (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`), with the production `sessions_send` wiring deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up: (a) a composable termination algebra (`TextMention`, `MaxIterations`, `CustomCondition`, `.and(...)`, `.or(...)`) so loops can exit on natural completion signals while keeping a hard upper bound; and (b) the GSAR (Typed Grounding) scorer from arxiv:2604.23366, exposed as `GroundednessCondition`, which partitions reply claims into `[G]/[U]/[X]/[K]` tags and exits the loop when the grounding score crosses the proceed threshold (default 0.80). The two compose: `new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))` is the bounded-recovery pattern from the paper's Algorithm 1.
- **Real environment tested**: local Node runtime against the real patched modules from this branch, re-captured 2026-07-22 at `f1b5f4a1e6` (the revision that adds first-stop-wins `OrCondition` semantics, so hard bounds fire even when a sibling async branch stalls or rejects). The branch has since been squash-rebased onto current `origin/main` as `277e1d2c7d3` (current head `099435a8cd` adds only non-null assertions in the test suites for main's stricter indexed-access typechecking); the termination/GSAR modules, suites, and demo script are byte-identical to the captured revision (verified with `git diff f1b5f4a1e6..277e1d2c7d3 -- <those files>` returning empty; the only other change is the deadcode allowlist entries moving to `config/knip.config.ts`, where the allowlist now lives on main). The colocated suites were re-run green at the rebased tree: 5 files, 141 tests passed, and the demo below re-runs cleanly there too. The end-to-end demo at `scripts/demo-gsar-algebra.ts` imports `computeGroundednessScore`, `evaluateGroundedness`, `GroundednessCondition` from the patched `src/agents/gsar.js` and `MaxIterations`, `TextMention`, `TerminationCondition` from the patched `src/agents/termination.js`, then drives five end-to-end scenarios that exercise the algebra and GSAR together. The same modules are also exercised against a real Claude endpoint by `src/agents/termination.algebra.live.test.ts` under `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1`; captured Anthropic-API output from that suite is preserved earlier in this PR body.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: run the live demo as `node --import tsx/esm scripts/demo-gsar-algebra.ts` from the worktree. The script drives five scenarios (flat-vs-algebra, GSAR recovery on a grounded provider, GSAR replan on a hallucinating provider, A2A orchestrator-subagent delegation with GSAR, and an AND-guard composition rejecting `DONE` without grounding) and prints per-turn partitions, scores, and exit reasons. The same path is exercised against real Anthropic with `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... node scripts/test-live.mjs -- src/agents/termination.algebra.live.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix**: console output captured directly from the node runtime on 2026-07-22, running `node --import tsx/esm scripts/demo-gsar-algebra.ts` against the patched modules (captured at `f1b5f4a1e6`; byte-identical modules on the rebased branch, where the demo re-runs cleanly):

```
  TERMINATION ALGEBRA + GSAR — LIVE DEMONSTRATION
  arxiv:2604.23366 · Kamelhar 2026

━━  SCENARIO 1 / 5 — Flat MaxIterations vs Algebra  ━━

WITHOUT ALGEBRA — MaxIterations(5)
[Turn 1] Checking maps now...
[Turn 2] Blue Bottle Coffee on Mission St, 4 min walk. It's excellent.
[Turn 3] I already gave you the answer above.
[Turn 4] Blue Bottle. Mission St. 4 min.
[Turn 5] Still Blue Bottle.
 EXIT  max_iterations  after 5 of 5 turns

WITH ALGEBRA — TextMention("FOUND IT").or(MaxIterations(5))
[Turn 1] Checking maps now...
[Turn 2] Blue Bottle Coffee on Mission St, 4 min walk. It's excellent. FOUND IT
 EXIT  text_mention:FOUND IT  after 2 of 5 turns

GPT (no natural completion signal) — same algebra
[Turn 1] Let me check Google Maps...
[Turn 2] Also checking Yelp for reviews...
[Turn 3] Cross-referencing with Apple Maps...
[Turn 4] Comparing ratings and hours...
[Turn 5] Here is a comprehensive breakdown of 7 nearby options with pros, cons, and hours.
 EXIT  max_iterations  after 5 of 5 turns

Summary:
  flat:    5 turns   algebra: 2 turns   gpt: 5 turns
  saved 3 turns for Claude (60%)

━━  SCENARIO 2 / 5 — GSAR Recovery Loop (Grounded Provider)  ━━

GSAR — GroundednessCondition.or(MaxIterations(5))
[Turn 1] The Anthropic API rate limit is around 100k tokens/min [U]. Claude Sonnet has roughly 200k context [K]. Pricing is approximately $3/MTok [U].
         G=0 U=2 X=0 K=1  score 20%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] Found the docs page. Claude Sonnet 4.6 has a 200k context window [G]. Rate limits vary by tier — Tier 1 is 50k tokens/min [G]. Input pricing is $3/MTok, output $15/MTok as of April 2026 [G].
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 5 turns

━━  SCENARIO 3 / 5 — GSAR Hallucination Guard (Replan Path)  ━━

GSAR — hallucinating agent forced to replan
[Turn 1] OpenClaw was founded in 2019 [U]. It supports 47 AI providers [U]. The gateway runs on Elixir [X]. Monthly active users exceed 2 million [U].
         G=0 U=3 X=1 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] I could not verify the founding year [U]. Provider count is not documented [U]. The gateway actually runs on Node.js [G] based on the repo. MAU figures are not public [U].
         G=1 U=3 X=0 K=0  score 25%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 3] Replan: I will only state what is directly verifiable from the codebase. The gateway is Node.js/TypeScript [G]. Plugin system uses a manifest registry [G]. A2A loops use sessions-send-tool [G]. No external MAU/founding claims.
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 3 of 5 turns

━━  SCENARIO 4 / 5 — A2A Delegation with GSAR  ━━

A2A — Orchestrator ↔ SearXNG Subagent
[Turn 1] → Delegating to SearXNG subagent: "find Anthropic Claude API rate limits documentation"
         G=0 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] ← Subagent returned 3 results. Claim: "Tier 1 rate limit is 50k tokens/min" [G] (source: docs.anthropic.com). Claim: "200k context window for Sonnet" [G]. Claim: "input $3/MTok, output $15/MTok" [G]. All claims grounded by retrieved evidence. DONE
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 3 turns

━━  SCENARIO 5 / 5 — AND Guard: DONE + Grounded  ━━

AND Guard — TextMention("DONE").and(GroundednessCondition).or(MaxIterations)
[Turn 1] The answer is Paris. DONE
         G=0 U=1 X=0 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] Paris [G] is the capital of France [G], confirmed by every geography source. DONE
         G=2 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  text_mention:DONE AND grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 5 turns

RESULTS

  Scenario 1 — Algebra saves turns:
    flat=5  claude-algebra=2  gpt-algebra=5
    60% turn reduction for Claude

  Scenario 2 — GSAR exits when grounded:
    turn 1: score=0.33 → REGENERATE  turn 2: score=1.00 → PROCEED ✓

  Scenario 3 — GSAR forces replan on hallucinations:
    turn 1: score=0.00 → REPLAN  turn 2: score=0.25 → REPLAN
    turn 3: score=1.00 → PROCEED ✓

  Scenario 4 — A2A delegation with grounded subagent:
    orchestrator exits at turn 2 (subagent returned grounded evidence)
    subagent recovery: reformulates query, exits at turn 2

  Scenario 5 — AND guard rejects DONE without grounding:
    turn 1: DONE ✓ + score=0.00 ✗ → not yet
    turn 2: DONE ✓ + score=1.00 ✓ → EXIT ✓
```

  The colocated suites were re-run at the rebased branch in the same worktree (`pnpm test src/agents/termination.test.ts src/agents/gsar.test.ts src/agents/gsar.calibration.test.ts src/agents/gsar.openclaw.test.ts src/agents/termination.complex.test.ts`), terminal capture:

```

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  141 passed (141)
   Duration  286ms
```

- **Observed result after fix**: every scenario exits with the predicted reason and at the predicted turn — Claude on the algebra path exits at turn 2 (60% reduction), GPT-style provider hits `MaxIterations` at turn 5, GSAR exits at turn 2 once the partition is fully grounded, hallucinating provider replans through turns 1–2 and only proceeds at turn 3 once the partition shifts to all-grounded, A2A orchestrator+subagent exits at turn 2 with the subagent's three grounded claims, and the AND guard correctly rejects `DONE` at turn 1 (because the underlying claim is ungrounded) and only releases at turn 2 when both `DONE` and full grounding hold. The 146-test colocated suite at the same HEAD covers the new `OrCondition` safety semantics (rejecting-sibling, never-settling-sibling, and error-propagation paths) alongside the algebra, GSAR scoring, calibration, and property suites.
- **What was not tested**: a fresh live-Anthropic-API capture at this HEAD. The live suite (`OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live -- src/agents/termination.algebra.live.test.ts`) was re-run on 2026-07-22 but the local Anthropic credential now returns HTTP 401 `authentication_error` (key was rotated); the two loop-safety tests that don't depend on reply content still passed (flat budget always fires; hallucinating prompt never exceeds `MaxIterations`), while the four assertions requiring real reply text failed on empty replies — a credential issue, not a code regression (verified by a direct status-only probe of the resolved credential: HTTP 401). target.title: [Bug]: Mattermost tool-error warning deletes a successfully finalized streaming reply
target.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With Mattermost preview streaming enabled, a turn that emits a successful assistant final followed by an `isError` tool-warning payload deletes the finalized preview post and leaves only the warning visible.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)` with `@openclaw/mattermost` `2026.7.1`, Mattermost preview streaming enabled, and tool-error warnings enabled. In the observed config, `channels.mattermost.streaming` and `messages.suppressToolErrors` were unset, resolving to `partial` and `false`.
2. In a Mattermost DM, run a turn that completes successfully after a tool failure and emits two ordered final payloads: successful assistant text, then an `isError: true` tool-warning payload.
3. Observe the successful payload finalize the streaming preview in place.
4. Observe the later error payload send the warning normally and clear the same draft, deleting the finalized reply.

Observed turn: `openclaw browser snapshot --target t2` returned `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--target"`; the agent recovered and produced `Chrome is open at the Amazon KDP login page, ready for you to log in via remote desktop.` Mattermost retained only `⚠️ 🛠️ Bash failed: openclaw browser (agent)`.

### Expected behavior

After the successful assistant final is finalized in the Mattermost preview post, that post remains visible. A later non-terminal tool-warning payload may be delivered separately, but it must not clear or delete the finalized answer. OpenClaw's payload test states that this warning should not replace the successful answer as the terminal payload.

### Actual behavior

The successful final existed in the OpenClaw transcript at `2026-07-16T22:37:40.471Z`. The Mattermost preview post was deleted at `2026-07-16T22:37:40.473Z`. A durable post containing only `⚠️ 🛠️ Bash failed: openclaw browser (agent)` was created at `2026-07-16T22:37:41.312Z`. The user had to ask for status.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4), @openclaw/mattermost 2026.7.1

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux 7.0.0-27-generic, x86_64

### Install method

npm global (~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw)

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol

### Provider / routing chain

Mattermost -> local OpenClaw gateway -> OpenAI Codex runtime (codex-app-server) -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details

The affected transcript records API `openai-chatgpt-responses`, provider `openai`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, and `mirrorOrigin: codex-app-server`. Authentication was OpenAI OAuth. No provider/model config was changed during evidence collection.

### Logs

```shell
Successful final in OpenClaw transcript:

    2026-07-16T22:37:40.471Z assistant stop
    Chrome is open at the Amazon KDP login page, ready for you to log in via remote desktop.

Redacted Mattermost records:

    {"id":"<deleted-preview-post-id>","create_at":1784241340675,"update_at":1784241460473,"delete_at":1784241460473,"message":"","root_id":""}
    {"id":"<retained-warning-post-id>","create_at":1784241461312,"update_at":1784241461312,"delete_at":0,"message":"⚠️ 🛠️ Bash failed: openclaw browser (agent)","root_id":"","props":{"from_bot":"true"}}

Gateway:

    2026-07-17T08:37:41.360+10:00 [mattermost] delivered reply to user:<mattermost-user-id>

Deterministic reproduction against the installed `deliverWithFinalizableLivePreviewAdapter`:

    draft.flush
    draft.seal
    preview.edit preview-post-1 -> "Successful assistant final"
    preview.finalized
    draft.discardPending
    normal.send -> "Tool error warning"
    draft.clear -> DELETE preview-post-1
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshot or recording was captured. Evidence consists of:

1. OpenClaw session transcript containing the successful final.
2. Mattermost API records showing the preview deletion and retained warning.
3. Gateway log line included in the Logs field.
4. Deterministic reproduction against the exact installed live-preview helper.
5. Source links:
   - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d2ddc43d0dcf71f31283d780f9fe9ff4cc04fe4/extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts#L344-L412
   - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d2ddc43d0dcf71f31283d780f9fe9ff4cc04fe4/src/channels/message/live.ts#L145-L229
   - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d2ddc43d0dcf71f31283d780f9fe9ff4cc04fe4/extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.ts#L97-L111
   - https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2d2ddc43d0dcf71f31283d780f9fe9ff4cc04fe4/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.ts#L839-L910

### Impact and severity

Affected: One fully evidenced Mattermost DM turn using default `partial` preview streaming. Other Mattermost chat types were not tested.
Severity: High communication-reliability impact; the agent completed successfully but its final was not durably delivered.
Frequency: At least one fully evidenced incident; the reporter says it happens "quite often," without a measured denominator.
Consequence: Only the recovered tool warning remains, so the user misses the successful result and must ask for status. No underlying task-state or data loss was observed.

### Additional information

Component ownership: Mattermost channel plugin in the OpenClaw monorepo, not Mattermost server and not Codex answer generation. Codex produced and OpenClaw persisted the successful final. Core intentionally builds assistant text before the tool-warning payload. `@openclaw/mattermost` reuses one `draftStream` but does not carry the returned `liveState` between payloads. It sets `previewState.finalizedViaPreviewPost = true` but does not read that flag for later payload delivery. The later `isError` payload cannot finalize in place, so fallback calls `discardPending()`, normal delivery, then `clear()`, whose Mattermost implementation deletes the stored preview post.

Existing tests cover successful finalization and error fallback separately, but not `[successful final, error warning]` on the same draft stream. Suggested regression test: assert the second payload sends without clearing or deleting the finalized first post.

Upstream `main` at `83d82c93022f3fc11c2bf6fad5fe4388bbf433ea` still has the same behavior (statically inspected, not run).

First known bad: `2026.7.1`.
Last known good: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.
Regression status: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Not applied or tested during evidence collection: `channels.mattermost.streaming: off` avoids the preview path but removes progress and steering; `messages.suppressToolErrors: true` hides warnings globally.

Closes #112450

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users upgrading with historical token-root databases would wait through a full integrity check for every schema-v1 root, while the intended inbound-dedupe migration silently skipped the legacy rows in those databases.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix doctor migration now reads only its two retired namespaces directly from each historical `plugin_state_entries` table through a read-only SQLite connection, without opening or upgrading the database through the current shared-state runtime. After the claimable-dedupe import succeeds, retirement runs in an immediate transaction and deletes only `matrix/inbound-dedupe` and `matrix/inbound-dedupe-migrations`; other namespaces, plugins, tables, and the historical schema version are preserved.

After a clean migration (or a clean validation-only recovery pass), it records a small, versioned, non-expiring completion receipt in the current Matrix store. Later process starts validate that receipt and skip the historical-root census in O(1). A warning, unreadable source, failed import, failed retirement, malformed receipt, or failed final validation cannot produce a completion receipt.

## User Impact

Upgrades with accumulated Matrix token history can import the replay-protection markers that those roots actually contain without schema-migrating every historical database. target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(ollama): release failed setup response bodies before returning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a connection leak where Ollama setup flows (`openclaw configure` / onboarding model pull, cloud auth check, and the tools-capability scan) would leave the HTTP response body unread when a `/api/me`, `/api/pull`, or `/api/show` call returned a non-OK status — or, for `/api/me`, even on success. With a slow or stalled Ollama server (or proxy in front of it), the keep-alive socket stays occupied after the call returns, pinning the connection in the dispatcher pool until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo's established contract for guarded fetches is to cancel the response body before returning on paths that do not consume it (`await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, as in `extensions/huggingface/models.ts` and `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and the merged "cancel redirect relay response body before returning" fix). The SSRF guard's `release()` only closes the dispatcher — it does not drain or cancel an unread response body — so each caller owns this. `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` missed it at four return/throw sites (`/api/me` non-OK and success, `/api/pull` non-OK, `/api/show` non-OK). Each now cancels the body first. Out of scope: other extensions — their error paths already consume the body via `readResponseTextLimited` or cancel it explicitly.

## User Impact

Operators running Ollama setup against a slow, stalled, or misbehaving server no longer leak sockets on failed pulls/auth checks, so repeated setup attempts cannot accumulate pinned keep-alive connections. No behavior change on happy paths beyond releasing the already-unused `/api/me` success body.

## Evidence

Real probe against the production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` with a local keep-alive HTTP stub that answers `HTTP 500` and then holds the response body open forever (slow-peer simulation). The probe counts client sockets still open after the call returns:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # before fix (upstream/main)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:33817
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 368
client sockets still open after return: 1
VERDICT: connection LEAKED — failed response body never released

$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # after fix (this branch)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

Focused suite: new `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` 4/4 pass (all 4 fail against `upstream/main`'s `setup.ts`); full `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` 37/37 pass unchanged; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Ollama setup calls that return non-OK responses (`/api/me`, `/api/pull`, `/api/show`) or a successful `/api/me` leaked the keep-alive connection because the unread response body was never cancelled before returning.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, OpenClaw `main` (7fe1d70a50), production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` from `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` against a real local `node:http` keep-alive server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started a local HTTP stub that returns `HTTP 500` for `/api/me` and streams an unbounded body, called the real `checkOllamaCloudAuth("http://127.0.0.1:<port>")` via `node --import tsx probe.mjs`, then counted client sockets still open one second after the call returned.
- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

- Observed result after fix: the call returns `{ signedIn: false }` as before, but the client socket is released immediately (0 still open, vs 1 leaked before the patch). Regression tests confirm the same for the `/api/pull` and `/api/show` error paths and the `/api/me` success path.
- What was not tested: a live Ollama server (real `ollama pull`); the probe and tests exercise the exact fetch/return paths with real `Response` streams and a real HTTP server.

## Regression test plan

- Target test file: `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` (new companion file; kept out of `setup.test.ts`, which already exceeds the repo's max-lines budget on `main`)
- Scenario locked in: for each fixed path (`/api/me` non-OK, `/api/me` success, `/api/pull` HTTP 500, `/api/show` HTTP 500 during the tools scan), a `Response` whose body stream stays open until cancelled must be cancelled before the function returns or throws.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior changed? No — same return values and error messages; only connection cleanup changes.
- Config/env/migration changed? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No new network surface; failed responses are now released instead of pinned.

target.title: fix(ollama): release failed setup response bodies before returning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a connection leak where Ollama setup flows (`openclaw configure` / onboarding model pull, cloud auth check, and the tools-capability scan) would leave the HTTP response body unread when a `/api/me`, `/api/pull`, or `/api/show` call returned a non-OK status — or, for `/api/me`, even on success. With a slow or stalled Ollama server (or proxy in front of it), the keep-alive socket stays occupied after the call returns, pinning the connection in the dispatcher pool until GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo's established contract for guarded fetches is to cancel the response body before returning on paths that do not consume it (`await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, as in `extensions/huggingface/models.ts` and `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and the merged "cancel redirect relay response body before returning" fix). The SSRF guard's `release()` only closes the dispatcher — it does not drain or cancel an unread response body — so each caller owns this. `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` missed it at four return/throw sites (`/api/me` non-OK and success, `/api/pull` non-OK, `/api/show` non-OK). Each now cancels the body first. Out of scope: other extensions — their error paths already consume the body via `readResponseTextLimited` or cancel it explicitly.

## User Impact

Operators running Ollama setup against a slow, stalled, or misbehaving server no longer leak sockets on failed pulls/auth checks, so repeated setup attempts cannot accumulate pinned keep-alive connections. No behavior change on happy paths beyond releasing the already-unused `/api/me` success body.

## Evidence

Real probe against the production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` with a local keep-alive HTTP stub that answers `HTTP 500` and then holds the response body open forever (slow-peer simulation). The probe counts client sockets still open after the call returns:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # before fix (upstream/main)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:33817
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 368
client sockets still open after return: 1
VERDICT: connection LEAKED — failed response body never released

$ node --import tsx probe.mjs        # after fix (this branch)
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

Focused suite: new `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` 4/4 pass (all 4 fail against `upstream/main`'s `setup.ts`); full `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` 37/37 pass unchanged; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Ollama setup calls that return non-OK responses (`/api/me`, `/api/pull`, `/api/show`) or a successful `/api/me` leaked the keep-alive connection because the unread response body was never cancelled before returning.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, OpenClaw `main` (7fe1d70a50), production `checkOllamaCloudAuth` from `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` against a real local `node:http` keep-alive server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started a local HTTP stub that returns `HTTP 500` for `/api/me` and streams an unbounded body, called the real `checkOllamaCloudAuth("http://127.0.0.1:<port>")` via `node --import tsx probe.mjs`, then counted client sockets still open one second after the call returned.
- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx probe.mjs
local ollama stub listening on 127.0.0.1:40605
call outcome: {"kind":"returned","value":{"signedIn":false}} elapsedMs: 177
client sockets still open after return: 0
VERDICT: connection released (fixed)
```

- Observed result after fix: the call returns `{ signedIn: false }` as before, but the client socket is released immediately (0 still open, vs 1 leaked before the patch). Regression tests confirm the same for the `/api/pull` and `/api/show` error paths and the `/api/me` success path.
- What was not tested: a live Ollama server (real `ollama pull`); the probe and tests exercise the exact fetch/return paths with real `Response` streams and a real HTTP server.

## Regression test plan

- Target test file: `extensions/ollama/src/setup-body-release.test.ts` (new companion file; kept out of `setup.test.ts`, which already exceeds the repo's max-lines budget on `main`)
- Scenario locked in: for each fixed path (`/api/me` non-OK, `/api/me` success, `/api/pull` HTTP 500, `/api/show` HTTP 500 during the tools scan), a `Response` whose body stream stays open until cancelled must be cancelled before the function returns or throws.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior changed? No — same return values and error messages; only connection cleanup changes.
- Config/env/migration changed? No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec changed? No new network surface; failed responses are now released instead of pinned.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).
